In such an environment, professional collaboration ceases, teacher stress and attrition skyrocket, and student emotional and academic well-being deteriorate. questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (b) है। शैक्षिक संगठन और विद्यालय संस्कृति के सिद्धांतकारों (जैसे पीटरसन और डील) के अनुसार, 'विषाक्त विद्यालय संस्कृति' (Toxic School Culture) एक ऐसा अस्वास्थ्यकर वातावरण है जहाँ शिक्षकों और प्रशासन के बीच अविश्वास, सूचनाओं को छिपाना, आपसी गुटबाजी, कटुता और असफलता के लिए एक-दूसरे पर दोष मढ़ने की प्रवृत्ति पाई जाती है। ऐसे माहौल में सहयोगात्मक शिक्षण समाप्त हो जाता है, शिक्षकों का मनोबल गिरता है और विद्यार्थियों का सर्वांगीण विकास बाधित होता है। विकल्प (a), (c) और (d) एक सकारात्मक, स्वस्थ और सहयोगी विद्यालयी संस्कृति के स्पष्ट लक्षण हैं।

questions.question_english: When conducting a strategic SWOT analysis for a public educational institution, which of the following factors constitutes an 'Opportunity'?
options_english: An exceptionally qualified, experienced, and dedicated internal teaching faculty
A newly sanctioned state grant designated for modernizing school digital and ICT infrastructure
Chronic electrical power instability and structural dilapidation within school premises
Elevated student dropout rates observed across secondary and higher secondary grades
questions.explanation_english: The correct answer is (b). In a SWOT analysis (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats), Strengths and Weaknesses are internal factors within the direct influence and control of the organization, whereas Opportunities and Threats are external environmental factors arising from the broader socio-economic, political, or technological landscape. A newly sanctioned government grant for upgrading ICT infrastructure represents an external, favorable condition that the school can leverage to expand its capabilities—hence, an Opportunity. Option (a) is incorrect because having dedicated and qualified teachers is an internal asset, which is a Strength. Option (c) is incorrect because power outages and building defects inside the school are internal operational deficiencies, which are Weaknesses. Option (d) is incorrect because internal dropout trends within the school's student body represent an internal institutional Weakness.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (b) है। रणनीतिक प्रबंधन के SWOT विश्लेषण में 'सामर्थ्य' (Strengths) और 'दुर्बलता' (Weaknesses) आंतरिक कारक होते हैं जो संस्था के नियंत्रण में होते हैं, जबकि 'अवसर' (Opportunities) और 'चुनौती' (Threats) बाह्य वातावरण से उत्पन्न होते हैं। आईसीटी उन्नयन के लिए सरकार द्वारा घोषित नवीन अनुदान एक सकारात्मक बाह्य कारक है जिसका लाभ उठाकर विद्यालय अपने शैक्षणिक स्तर में सुधार कर सकता है, अतः यह एक 'अवसर' है। विकल्प (a) गलत है क्योंकि योग्य शिक्षक विद्यालय की आंतरिक शक्ति हैं। विकल्प (c) गलत है क्योंकि बिजली और भवन की समस्या आंतरिक कमजोरी है। विकल्प (d) गलत है क्योंकि विद्यार्थियों की उच्च शाला-त्याग दर विद्यालय की आंतरिक दुर्बलता को दर्शाती है।

Harnessing these external resources enables educational institutions to upgrade technological infrastructure, expand academic capacity, and achieve strategic objectives.

questions.question_english: In supervisory theory, which of the following best defines the primary orientation of 'Corrective Supervision'?
options_english: Anticipating emerging curriculum challenges and designing proactive institutional prevention strategies
Detecting specific instructional mistakes or procedural shortcomings and providing targeted remedial guidance
Fostering uninhibited pedagogical experimentation, action research, and novel classroom innovation
Granting instructional faculty complete laissez-faire autonomy in the complete absence of supervisory oversight
questions.explanation_english: The correct answer is (b). Corrective supervision is a supervisory approach focused on identifying immediate, noticeable pedagogical flaws, errors, or classroom management deficiencies in a teacher's practice and providing direct, targeted remedial suggestions to rectify them. While more helpful than purely punitive inspection, corrective supervision primarily aims to eliminate observed defects and restore baseline educational standards rather than proactively anticipating difficulties (preventive) or promoting novel methodologies (creative). Option (a) defines Preventive Supervision. Option (c) defines Creative Supervision. Option (d) describes Laissez-faire or non-directive supervision.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (b) है। 'सुधारात्मक पर्यवेक्षण' (करेक्टिव सुपरविजन) का मुख्य उद्देश्य कक्षा शिक्षण में उत्पन्न होने वाली विशिष्ट त्रुटियों, कमियों या प्रक्रियात्मक दोषों को इंगित करना और उन्हें दूर करने के लिए प्रत्यक्ष उपचारात्मक मार्गदर्शन व सुझाव देना है। यह पर्यवेक्षक को एक सुधारक के रूप में प्रस्तुत करता है जो मानकों को बहाल करने के लिए तत्काल प्रतिपुष्टि प्रदान करता है। विकल्प (a) निवारक पर्यवेक्षण से संबंधित है। विकल्प (c) सृजनात्मक पर्यवेक्षण का लक्षण है। विकल्प (d) अहस्तक्षेपवादी पर्यवेक्षण को दर्शाता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Identifying specific performance errors and providing direct remedial guidance.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Corrective supervision focuses on identifying specific errors, shortcomings, or instructional deficiencies in classroom practices and offering targeted remedial support. Rather than waiting for long-term evaluation cycles, this approach directly addresses observed mistakes to restore teaching standards. Supervisors provide constructive feedback and practical corrective techniques, helping teachers rectify specific procedural or pedagogical flaws efficiently and maintain educational quality.

questions.question_english: In the context of educational governance and organizational administration, the ISO 9000 series of standards is fundamentally associated with:
options_english: Quality management systems and institutional quality assurance frameworks
Environmental sustainability, ecological safety, and green institutional benchmarks
Information technology hardware specifications and network infrastructure standards
Nutritional dietary benchmarks and food safety standards for institutional meal programs
questions.explanation_english:
The International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 9000 series is an internationally recognized family of standards dedicated to Quality Management Systems (QMS). In educational institutions, implementing ISO 9000 (such as ISO 9001) helps schools establish standardized administrative workflows, documented standard operating procedures (SOPs), rigorous pedagogical auditing mechanisms, continuous stakeholder feedback loops, and systematic continuous quality improvement protocols. This enhances institutional efficiency, academic excellence, and accountability to learners, parents, and regulatory bodies.
- Option B is incorrect because environmental management and ecological sustainability standards are governed by the ISO 14000 series (specifically ISO 14001).
- Option C is incorrect because information security, IT hardware, and data management are governed by the ISO/IEC 27000 series.
- Option D is incorrect because food safety and nutritional management systems are covered under the ISO 22000 series.
questions.explanation_hindi:
अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मानकीकरण संगठन (आई.एस.ओ.) की 9000 शृंखला गुणवत्ता प्रबंधन प्रणाली से संबंधित वैश्विक मानकों का एक समुच्चय है। किसी शैक्षणिक संस्थान में आई.एस.ओ. 9000 के मानकों को लागू करने से प्रशासनिक प्रक्रियाओं में मानकीकरण आता है, मानक संचालन प्रक्रियाएं निर्धारित होती हैं, शिक्षण-अधिगम गुणवत्ता का नियमित लेखापरीक्षण होता है और निरंतर सुधार की संस्कृति स्थापित होती है।
- विकल्प (B) गलत है क्योंकि पर्यावरणीय प्रबंधन और पारिस्थितिकी सुरक्षा के मानक आई.एस.ओ. 14000 शृंखला के अंतर्गत आते हैं।
- विकल्प (C) गलत है क्योंकि सूचना सुरक्षा और डेटा प्रबंधन प्रणाली के मानक आई.एस.ओ./आई.ई.सी. 27000 शृंखला द्वारा शासित होते हैं।
- विकल्प (D) गलत है क्योंकि खाद्य सुरक्षा और आहार प्रबंधन मानक आई.एस.ओ. 22000 शृंखला से संबंधित हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Quality management and quality assurance standards.

questions.question_english: Which of the following is classified as a genuine ‘Motivator’ (rather than an extrinsic hygiene factor) in Frederick Herzberg’s Two-Factor Theory?
options_english: Physical working conditions and facilities in the school environment
Quality of interpersonal relations maintained with the school Principal
Base financial salary package and annual incremental pay raises
Personal achievement and professional recognition for good work
questions.explanation_english: The correct answer is (d). In Herzberg's Dual-Factor Theory, 'Motivators' (satisfiers) are intrinsic factors derived directly from the content of the work and individual psychological growth. Examples include personal achievement, recognition, responsibility, meaningful challenging work, and advancement opportunities. These intrinsic motivators actively generate job satisfaction and drive individuals toward superior commitment and performance. In contrast, physical working conditions (Option a), interpersonal relationships with superiors (Option b), and basic financial salary/increments (Option c) are extrinsic 'Hygiene Factors' (or maintenance factors) that merely prevent workplace dissatisfaction without fostering genuine intrinsic motivation.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (d) है। फ्रेडरिक हर्ज़बर्ग के द्वि-कारक सिद्धांत में 'अभिप्रेरक' (Motivators) वे आंतरिक कारक हैं जो सीधे कार्य की विषय-वस्तु, कार्य की सार्थकता और व्यक्ति के व्यक्तिगत व व्यावसायिक विकास से जुड़े होते हैं। इनमें व्यक्तिगत उपलब्धि, उत्कृष्ट कार्य की पहचान व मान्यता, दायित्व, और पदोन्नति के अवसर शामिल हैं। ये कारक कर्मचारियों में सक्रिय रूप से उच्च कार्य-संतुष्टि उत्पन्न करते हैं और उन्हें उत्कृष्ट प्रदर्शन हेतु प्रेरित करते हैं। इसके विपरीत, भौतिक कार्य-दशाएँ (विकल्प a), प्रधानाचार्य के साथ पारस्परिक संबंध (विकल्प b) तथा बुनियादी वेतन व वार्षिक वेतन वृद्धि (विकल्प c) बाह्य 'आरोग्य कारक' (Hygiene Factors) हैं, जो केवल कार्य-असंतोष को दूर रखते हैं किंतु कर्मचारियों को आंतरिक रूप से अभिप्रेरित नहीं करते।

questions.question_english: Which contemporary educational leadership model argues that leadership is not the monopoly of the Principal, but is rather a shared construct extending to teachers, staff, and even students?

questions.explanation_english: The correct answer is (d). questions.explanation_english: The correct answer is (b). Abraham Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs structures human motives into a five-tier ascending pyramid: physiological needs at the base, followed by safety and security, social belongingness, esteem and status, and finally self-actualization at the apex. Individuals seek self-actualization only after lower-order deficiency needs are substantially satisfied. Option (a), esteem needs, occupies the fourth tier just below the peak. Option (c), social belonging needs, resides on the third tier. Option (d), safety and security needs, occupies the second tier directly above basic physiological survival needs.

questions.question_english: In educational management, if a teacher is required to report simultaneously to two different Vice-Principals who issue contradictory instructions, which classical management principle articulated by Henri Fayol is directly violated?
options_english: Unity of Command
Span of Control
Scalar Chain
Division of Work
questions.explanation_english:
Henri Fayol formulated the 14 Principles of Management, among which the principle of 'Unity of Command' (Unité de commandement) explicitly states that an individual employee should receive orders from, and report directly to, one and only one superior. When a teacher is subjected to dual supervision from two Vice-Principals issuing conflicting directives, unity of command is breached. This violation leads to role ambiguity, stress, administrative friction, shifting of blame, and organizational dysfunction.
- Option B is incorrect because 'Span of Control' refers to the optimal number of subordinates that a single manager or supervisor can efficiently oversee.
- Option C is incorrect because 'Scalar Chain' refers to the unbroken line of authority running from the highest executive down to the lowest ranks of an organization.
- Option D is incorrect because 'Division of Work' (specialization) pertains to breaking down complex operations into specialized tasks to maximize efficiency and expertise.

- विकल्प (B) गलत है क्योंकि 'नियंत्रण का विस्तार' एक अधिकारी के प्रत्यक्ष पर्यवेक्षण में काम करने वाले अधीनस्थों की संख्या से संबंधित है।

questions.question_english: Within the framework of Total Quality Management (TQM) applied to educational systems, the continuous improvement PDCA cycle popularized by W. Edwards Deming comprises which four sequential phases?
options_english: Plan, Delegate, Control, Assess
Process, Design, Coordinate, Achieve
Prioritize, Direct, Communicate, Align
Plan, Do, Check, Act
questions.explanation_english:
The correct answer is (d). The PDCA cycle (also known as the Deming Cycle or Shewhart Cycle) is a four-step iterative management method used in Total Quality Management (TQM) for continuous process improvement. The stages are:
1. Plan: Identify a problem or improvement opportunity, establish objectives, and formulate a targeted action plan.
2. Do: Implement the plan and test the proposed changes on a small, pilot scale.
3. Check: Monitor, measure, and analyze the resulting data against predetermined criteria to evaluate effectiveness.
4. Act: Standardize successful interventions across the institution, or refine and restart the cycle if goals were not met.
Options (a), (b), and (c) are incorrect combinations of administrative words that do not represent the established Deming PDCA quality framework.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर (d) है। संपूर्ण गुणवत्ता प्रबंधन (TQM) में 'PDCA चक्र' (जिसे डेमिंग चक्र भी कहा जाता है) निरंतर गुणवत्ता सुधार की एक चक्रीय कार्यपद्धति है। इसके चार चरण हैं:
1. Plan (योजना बनाएं): सुधार के क्षेत्र की पहचान करना और कार्ययोजना निर्धारित करना।
2. Do (करें): योजना को छोटे स्तर या प्रायोगिक तौर पर लागू करना।
3. Check (जांचें): परिणामों का परीक्षण और विश्लेषण करना कि क्या वे लक्ष्यों के अनुरूप हैं।
4. Act (सुधारें/लागू करें): सफल परिवर्तनों को मानक प्रक्रिया के रूप में अपनाना अथवा कमियों को दूर कर नए सिरे से चक्र प्रारंभ करना।
विकल्प (a), (b) और (c) मनगढ़ंत शब्द युग्म हैं और डेमिंग के इस मान्य गुणवत्ता चक्र का प्रतिनिधित्व नहीं करते हैं।

questions.question_english: Herbert Simon's model of 'Bounded Rationality' in administrative decision-making asserts that:
options_english: Human cognitive limits, information deficits, and temporal constraints prevent decision-makers from achieving purely rational optimization
Educational administrators possess perfect information and computational clarity to arrive at universally flawless decisions
Administrative decisions must rely exclusively on subjective emotional intuition rather than analytical evidence
Rationality in school governance is bounded exclusively by the physical budgetary limits of the contingency fund
questions.explanation_english: The correct answer is (a). Herbert Simon introduced the concept of 'Bounded Rationality' to challenge the classical economic view of the completely rational decision-maker ('economic man'). Simon argued that in real-world administrative environments, human decision-makers face cognitive limitations, incomplete and ambiguous information, and severe time constraints. Consequently, administrators cannot examine all possible alternatives or foresee all outcomes to reach an absolute optimum. Instead, they operate within 'bounded rationality' and practice 'satisficing'—selecting an alternative that is good enough and meets satisfactory criteria. Option (b) is incorrect because Simon specifically rejects the notion of omniscience or perfect decision-making. Option (c) is incorrect because Simon does not advocate relying purely on intuition over empirical data; he analyzes the constraints on analytical rationality. Option (d) is incorrect because 'bounded rationality' relates to cognitive and informational constraints, not just monetary budgetary limits.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (a) है। नोबेल पुरस्कार विजेता हर्बर्ट साइमन ने 'सीमित तार्किकता' का सिद्धांत प्रस्तुत कर यह स्पष्ट किया कि वास्तविक प्रशासनिक परिस्थितियों में कोई भी व्यक्ति पूर्णतः तर्कसंगत निर्णय नहीं ले सकता। निर्णयकर्ता के पास सूचना की अपूर्णता, जटिलता को संसाधित करने की सीमित मानसिक क्षमता (संज्ञानात्मक सीमाएँ) और समय का अभाव होता है। इसलिए, प्रशासक सर्वोत्तम विकल्प खोजने के बजाय 'संतोषप्रद' विकल्प चुनते हैं जो उस स्थिति के लिए पर्याप्त और व्यावहारिक हो। विकल्प (b) गलत है क्योंकि यह पूर्ण तार्किकता का अवास्तविक दावा करता है। विकल्प (c) गलत है क्योंकि साइमन अंतर्ज्ञान पर निर्भर रहने की वकालत नहीं करते। विकल्प (d) गलत है क्योंकि सीमित तार्किकता का संबंध मानव संज्ञान और सूचना से है, न कि केवल बजटीय सीमाओं से।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Human cognitive limitations and time constraints prevent fully rational decision-making.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Herbert Simon introduced the concept of bounded rationality to highlight that human decision-makers rarely achieve complete objectivity. Administrators operate under constraints such as incomplete information, cognitive processing limits, and restricted time frames. Consequently, leaders do not seek absolute optimal solutions but instead make satisficing choices that meet acceptable operational standards given the environmental constraints present.

Consider the following sequential stages of the Clinical Supervision process:
I. Direct Classroom Observation
II. Pre-observation Planning Conference
III. Observational Analysis and Strategy Formulation
IV. Post-observation Feedback Conference
Which of the following represents the correct chronological progression of these stages?
options_english: II, I, III, IV
I, II, IV, III
II, III, I, IV

questions.explanation_english:
The correct answer is (a). The Clinical Supervision cycle formulated by Morris Cogan and Robert Goldhammer adheres to a rigorous chronological sequence:
1. Pre-observation Conference (II): The supervisor and teacher meet prior to instruction to establish rapport, clarify instructional goals, delineate lesson objectives, and agree upon specific observational foci.
2. Classroom Observation (I): The supervisor enters the classroom and systematically records objective, factual behavioral data as agreed.
3. Analysis and Strategy Formulation (III): The supervisor reviews and categorizes the gathered classroom data, identifying meaningful pedagogical patterns and structuring an empathetic conference agenda.
4. Post-observation Conference (IV): The supervisor and educator meet collegially to review the empirical findings, discuss reflective insights, and formulate targeted instructional improvements.
Therefore, the correct chronological order is II, I, III, IV.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर (a) है। कोगन और गोल्डहैमर द्वारा विकसित नैदानिक पर्यवेक्षण का चक्र एक सुव्यवस्थित तार्किक और कालानुक्रमिक क्रम का अनुसरण करता है:
1. अवलोकन-पूर्व संगोष्ठी (II): कक्षा में जाने से पहले शिक्षक और पर्यवेक्षक बैठक कर पाठ के उद्देश्यों, शिक्षण रणनीतियों और अवलोकन के विशिष्ट बिंदुओं को तय करते हैं।
2. कक्षा अवलोकन (I): पर्यवेक्षक कक्षा में बैठकर पूर्व-निर्धारित बिंदुओं पर वस्तुनिष्ठ आँकड़े एकत्र करता है।
3. विश्लेषण एवं रणनीति निर्माण (III): संगोष्ठी से पहले पर्यवेक्षक एकत्रित आँकड़ों का विश्लेषण करता है और प्रतिपुष्टि की रणनीति बनाता है।
4. अवलोकन-पश्चात संगोष्ठी (IV): अंत में, शिक्षक और पर्यवेक्षक मिलकर आँकड़ों पर सहयोगात्मक चर्चा करते हैं और भविष्य के शिक्षण सुधार की योजना बनाते हैं।
अतः सही क्रम II, I, III, IV है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) II, I, III, IV

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): In LMX Theory, followers in the ‘in-group’ generally experience higher job satisfaction and lower turnover intentions.
Reason (R): In-group members have high-quality exchanges with the leader, receiving more resources, support, and autonomy.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

questions.explanation_english: The correct answer is (a). George Graen's Leader-Member Exchange (LMX) Theory conceptualizes leadership as a series of unique dyadic relationships between a leader and individual followers, resulting in the formation of an 'in-group' and an 'out-group'. In-group subordinates enjoy high-quality developmental exchanges characterized by mutual respect, trust, bidirectional influence, and shared responsibilities. Consequently, leaders allocate more administrative resources, personalized mentorship, challenging assignments, and decision-making latitude to in-group members, making Reason (R) true. Because this enriched, supportive interpersonal dynamic directly enhances job satisfaction, organizational commitment, and retention, Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A). questions.question_english: In teacher performance appraisal and supervisory evaluation, the 'Halo Effect' refers to the cognitive bias wherein:
options_english: An appraiser rates all teaching personnel uniformly as 'Average' to avoid interpersonal conflict or administrative scrutiny
An evaluator assesses an educator's competence based almost exclusively on their most recent conduct and achievements
An appraiser's favorable impression of a single outstanding positive trait unduly inflates their ratings across all other performance dimensions
An appraiser deliberately assigns substandard marks to a subordinate due to personal grievance or underlying prejudice
questions.explanation_english:
The 'Halo Effect', first identified empirically by psychologist Edward Thorndike in 1920, is a common cognitive bias in performance appraisals where an evaluator's global impression or positive assessment of one specific characteristic (such as exceptional punctuality, pleasant demeanor, or articulate verbal skills) disproportionately influences and inflates their rating of the individual across completely unrelated competencies (such as lesson planning, classroom management, or subject mastery). This cognitive distortion undermines objectivity and distorts professional developmental feedback.
- Option A is incorrect because rating everyone uniformly in the middle to avoid making difficult evaluations is known as the 'Central Tendency Bias'.
- Option B is incorrect because judging an employee's annual performance based predominantly on recent incidents rather than the entire appraisal period is known as the 'Recency Bias' (or recency error).
- Option D is incorrect because unfairly downgrading an employee due to prejudice or personal dislike is an instance of appraiser bias, personal prejudice, or the opposite 'Horns Effect'.

- विकल्प (A) गलत है क्योंकि कठोर निर्णयों से बचने के लिए सभी को बीच की औसत रेटिंग देना 'केंद्रीय प्रवृत्ति पूर्वाग्रह' कहलाता है।
- विकल्प (B) गलत है क्योंकि पूरे वर्ष के बजाय केवल हाल की घटनाओं के आधार पर राय बनाना 'हालिया प्रभाव' कहलाता है।
- विकल्प (D) गलत है क्योंकि किसी एक नकारात्मक पहलू या व्यक्तिगत दुर्भावना के कारण संपूर्ण मूल्यांकन को खराब कर देना 'हॉर्न्स प्रभाव' कहलाता है।

Read the following statements regarding the four components of Transformational Leadership (the Four I’s):
I. Idealized Influence: Serving as a charismatic role model.
II. Inspirational Motivation: Articulating a compelling vision of the future.
III. Intellectual Stimulation: Encouraging innovation and critical thinking.

options_english: I and II only
I, II and III only
III and IV only

questions.explanation_english: The correct answer is (d). Bernard M. Bass and Bruce J. Avolio established that Transformational Leadership operates through four distinct, interrelated components known as the 'Four I's': (1) Idealized Influence—the leader acts as an ethical, charismatic role model whom followers respect, admire, and seek to emulate; (2) Inspirational Motivation—the leader articulates an appealing, optimistic vision of the future that energizes followers and gives meaning to their work; (3) Intellectual Stimulation—the leader challenges existing norms, encourages creativity, and empowers subordinates to solve problems innovatively without fear of ridicule; and (4) Individualized Consideration—the leader provides personalized mentoring and coaching, recognizing and nurturing each follower's individual developmental needs and talents. Because all four statements are accurately described, Option (d) is correct.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (d) है। बर्नार्ड बास और ब्रूस एवोलियो द्वारा प्रतिपादित रूपांतरणकारी नेतृत्व (Transformational Leadership) के चार केंद्रीय स्तंभ हैं, जिन्हें फोर 'I' (4 Is) कहा जाता है: (1) आदर्शित प्रभाव (Idealized Influence)—नेता उच्च नैतिक मूल्यों और व्यक्तिगत करिश्मे का प्रदर्शन कर अनुयायियों के लिए एक रोल मॉडल के रूप में कार्य करता है; (2) प्रेरणादायक अभिप्रेरणा (Inspirational Motivation)—नेता भविष्य का एक स्पष्ट, उत्साहवर्धक और साझा दृष्टिकोण (विज़न) प्रस्तुत करता है जो सभी को प्रेरित करता है; (3) बौद्धिक उद्दीपन (Intellectual Stimulation)—नेता अनुयायियों को स्थापित मान्यताओं पर प्रश्न उठाने, स्वतंत्र चिंतन करने और समस्याओं के नए रचनात्मक समाधान खोजने के लिए प्रोत्साहित करता है; तथा (4) व्यक्तिगत ध्यान (Individualized Consideration)—नेता प्रत्येक अनुयायी की व्यक्तिगत क्षमताओं और विकास संबंधी आवश्यकताओं को समझकर एक परामर्शदाता/मेंटर के रूप में उनका मार्गदर्शन करता है। अतः सभी चारों कथन सत्य हैं।

questions.explanation_english:
On the Blake and Mouton Managerial Grid (Leadership Grid), managerial behavior is mapped on a 9x9 matrix along two independent dimensions: 'Concern for Production' (horizontal axis) and 'Concern for People' (vertical axis). The (5,5) coordinate represents 'Middle-of-the-Road Management' (Organization Man Management). A leader at this position adopts a philosophy of compromise and satisficing: balancing the necessity to get educational work done with maintaining staff morale at a tolerable, satisfactory level. Such leaders avoid conflict and maintain institutional stability, but rarely inspire extraordinary achievement or transformative innovation.
- Option A is incorrect because coordinate (1,1), 'Impoverished Management', represents minimal concern for both production and people.
- Option B is incorrect because coordinate (1,9), 'Country Club Management', represents high concern for people combined with low concern for production.

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): During the 'Change' (Moving) phase of Kurt Lewin's Three-Stage Model of Change, school administrators must anticipate and accommodate a temporary dip in institutional performance.
Reason (R): Navigating new pedagogical practices and administrative protocols requires staff to traverse a learning curve and exit familiar comfort zones, temporarily elevating confusion, cognitive load, and inefficiency.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is true, but (R) is false
(A) is false, but (R) is true
questions.explanation_english:
Kurt Lewin's classic Three-Stage Model of Change consists of Unfreezing, Changing (or Moving), and Refreezing. During the 'Change' phase, the organization implements new structures, curriculum frameworks, or management procedures. It is well-documented in change management theory (often illustrated by the 'J-curve' of change) that organizational productivity and performance temporarily decline during this phase. This dip occurs precisely because employees and educators are abandoning established, comfortable habits and struggling with the steep learning curve of new tools, which temporarily heightens cognitive burden, stress, operational errors, and transitional inefficiency.
